The section 'Why s<Wm' reproduces the paper's telescoping count. Climbing 0 to m on every wire gives Wm; the X_a line sources and the Y_a sinks of dimension m-1 save 2N; the shrinking edges add 2L; the bit-network source sign adds one rank per X_a. This gives s_b=W_b m-(N-2L_b) and s_c=W_c m-(2N-2L_c), with L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 both below 1/2, as in Lemma motif-residuals and Props bit/complex-motif-interface.

errors.quote: The branching factor is the fixed label-space dimension $m=h^3=10^6$
errors.problem: The number of children per node, s, is the branching factor. m is the factor by which the parameter shrinks per level, and it sets the depth log_m f. The paper says 'the branching factor s is fixed and the depth is at most ceil(log_m d)'.

errors.quote: So any fixed $\tau<1$ with $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $\mathcal C(f)=O(f^\tau)$
errors.problem: This also needs tau>0, which the paper assumes (tau in (0,1)). For s/W<=1 the sum is O(log f) or O(1), and that is O(f^tau) only when tau>0 (tau>=0 if s/W<1).

errors.quote: its frame changes are binary changes of basis, done by chunk interchanges at cost $O(V((fK)^\tau+1))$ per node
errors.problem: This conflates two different costs. In the paper, an edge's frame change C_V C_U^{-1} is a product of translation kernels, and these are carried out by the s recursive calls. The O(V((eK)^tau+1)) term is the per-node overhead: the binary changes of basis and their inverses (row additions via the packed selected-bit addition), plus the gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly.
